expertise_paragraph: During his PhD, Umar independently built specialized lab equipment, including an EGaIn-based system for studying molecular junctions and STM / MCBJ break-junction setups for measuring electrical properties at the nanoscale, designed using AutoCAD Inventor. He developed and 3D-printed multiple prototypes before converging on the most stable designs, and wrote custom LabVIEW software to control the instruments and automate data analysis — including algorithms to extract meaningful correlations and key metrics from noisy data, work that has since been published. While LabVIEW remains his primary tool, he is comfortable moving to Python for future projects. He is also familiar with quantum-mechanical calculations from his master's work, mainly using Gaussian with some early work in SIESTA, though transport calculations were outside the scope of his PhD, which focused on experiment. His chemistry background spans UV-Vis and fluorescence spectroscopy, atomic force microscopy, electrochemical methods, and early-stage synthesis, complemented by an undergraduate foundation in biology and biochemistry. Overall, he combines hands-on engineering — building instruments and writing control software — with depth across chemistry and biology, allowing him to work across materials science and the life sciences.

Instrumentation & Spectroscopy: Instrumentation development — STM-BJ, MCBJ, ensemble molecular junctions
